title: ULPPL - Low Volume Powerbuilding
author: Dr. M Khader Shah
desc:
12-week powerbuilding program built around a simple philosophy: practice the competition lifts with controlled fatigue while pushing hypertrophy work hard and efficiently.
The powerlifting component uses squat, bench press, and deadlift with percentage-based loading and deliberately conservative RPEs. Early weeks prioritize technique, consistency, bar path, bracing, setup, and competition-specific execution rather than turning the main lifts into hypertrophy work. Intensity gradually increases across the block while maintaining control and avoiding unnecessary grinders.
The hypertrophy component follows a low-volume, high-intensity approach. Most exercises use warm-up sets followed by exactly two hard working sets: one main set of 4–8 reps at 0–1 RIR, followed by one back-off set of 6–10 reps at 1–2 RIR. Selected exercises use only one hard set where needed to keep weekly muscle volume around the target without adding junk volume.
The program trains all major muscle groups across five days while combining direct hypertrophy work with the additional stimulus from the competition lifts.
The goal: maximize strength and muscle gain while keeping training efficient, recoverable, and technically focused—rather than accumulating fatigue simply for the sake of more volume.
